solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Difficult problem learner assimilated by heart (7)

indicators.note: the heart word takes the learner into itself

blocks.note: ticker is slang for the heart

annotation.surface: A struggling student is finally taking a hard lesson to heart.
annotation.walkthrough: Heart reads as feeling, as in taking a lesson to heart, but it is the organ, known in slang by the sound it makes.
annotation.definitionFit: A tickler is a puzzling or delicate problem, a poser.

entries.clue: Hard drinker served up moonshine (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending letters up turns them round

annotation.surface: A heavy drinker is being served illicit homemade spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Moonshine here is not bootleg liquor but its other sense, foolish talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Besides bootleg spirit, moonshine carries the sense of foolish, fanciful talk, which is the British slang meaning of tosh.

entries.clue: Appropriate to have unclosed trunk tossed outside Savoy? (7)

indicators.note: the first word is made to hold what follows
the trunk word loses its closing letter
the shortened trunk goes round the first word

blocks.note: a caber is the tree trunk tossed at Highland games; drop its last letter R
to bag is to appropriate, take for oneself

annotation.surface: Someone is sneaking a trunk into the grand Savoy hotel in London.
annotation.walkthrough: Savoy looks like the London hotel, but the question mark marks it as an example: a Savoy is a crinkly-leaved cabbage. A caber is the log thrown in the Scottish sport of caber tossing.
annotation.definitionFit: Savoy is a variety of cabbage, so it defines by example.

entries.clue: Pounds advanced to secure leather and wool (5)

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the leather word inside them

blocks.note: to leather and to lam both mean to thrash

annotation.surface: A merchant pays money up front to buy hides and fleece.
annotation.walkthrough: Leather is the verb, to beat, not the material; the surface of hides and fleece hides that.
annotation.definitionFit: Llama is a fibre sold as wool, spun from the animal's coat.

entries.clue: Recheck less exposed cracks in most piping (8)

indicators.note: the word is stripped of its outer letters
the short piece breaks into the longer word

blocks.note: to re-edit is to go over again
LESS with its outer L and S removed

annotation.surface: An inspector goes over the plumbing again, finding fewer visible cracks in the pipes.
annotation.walkthrough: Piping is a thin high voice, not plumbing; a reedy voice is thin and shrill.
annotation.definitionFit: Reediest means shrillest or thinnest in tone, the most piping.

entries.clue: In club, drop shot of ecstasy (7)

indicators.note: the E is let go from the shot word

blocks.note: a shot of colour is a tinge
E = the drug ecstasy; removed from TINGE

annotation.surface: In a nightclub, someone knocks back a dose of ecstasy.
annotation.walkthrough: Club, drop and shot all look like nightlife, but the definition is the lone word In: a cricketer who is in is batting.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket, the side or player who is in is batting.

entries.clue: Thin fencing erected at field of flowers? (6)

indicators.note: the thin word surrounds the turned piece like a fence
in a down entry, raising letters turns them round

annotation.surface: A flimsy fence has been put up around a meadow of flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: A field of flowers is not a meadow here but a field of study: the science of plants.
annotation.definitionFit: Botany is the academic field that studies plants, flowers included.

entries.clue: International pilot heading for Chicago entering course to the US (4,5)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Chicago
the C goes inside the course word

blocks.note: a pilot scheme is a test
Americans call the school subject math

annotation.surface: An international airline pilot is on the approach to Chicago.
annotation.walkthrough: International is a noun here: a match between national teams. A Test match is an international cricket match.
annotation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international fixture, especially in cricket.

entries.clue: Counter popular bible passage (7)

blocks.note: a verse is a numbered passage of scripture

annotation.surface: A preacher offers a well-loved scripture reading as a rebuttal.
annotation.walkthrough: Counter looks like a noun or verb, a shop counter or to rebut, but it works as an adjective meaning opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: Counter as an adjective means opposite, and so does inverse.

entries.clue: Greek keeping isolated housing touched up for posh people (10)

indicators.note: the Greek abbreviation holds everything else
the isolated word holds the touched word
in a down entry, the combined piece reads upward

blocks.note: Gk is the standard abbreviation for Greek

annotation.surface: A Greek keeps a remote house that has been redecorated for wealthy clients.
annotation.walkthrough: Touched up looks like a paint job, but it splits: touched gives FELT and up turns LO-FELT-NE round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gentlefolk is an old-fashioned word for people of good birth and breeding, the upper classes.

entries.clue: Base can just be forming a foundation (9)

indicators.note: base means corrupt, so the letters that follow are debased

annotation.surface: A builder says the base could just about serve as the foundation.
annotation.walkthrough: Base sits where a definition usually goes and means foundation too, which makes it look like the definition; it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Subjacent means lying underneath, as a foundation does.

entries.clue: Number days before turning eighteen at last (5)

indicators.note: the days word is turned round
takes the final letter of eighteen

blocks.note: eves are the days before events

annotation.surface: Someone counts the days before they come of age at eighteen.
annotation.walkthrough: An eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve, so days before gives EVES.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: seven is one number among many, the kind of broad category setters use for any numeral.

entries.clue: 1 or 2 perhaps are reported to be aboard mobile air ambulance (6,7)

indicators.note: the word are is taken for its sound, the letter R
R goes inside the jumbled letters
the letters of air ambulance move about

blocks.note: the letter R is pronounced like are

annotation.surface: Patients one and two are said to be on board a mobile air ambulance.
annotation.walkthrough: 1 and 2 look like patients or cases, but they are the digits themselves, written as Arabic numerals.
annotation.definitionFit: 1 and 2 are examples of Arabic numerals, as opposed to Roman I and II.

entries.clue: In local cast, see Belgian who’s dictionally informal (10)

indicators.note: the next pieces go inside the jumbled word
the letters of local are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: qui is French for who, spoken in Belgium

annotation.surface: In a local theatre production, a Belgian actor is being chatty.
annotation.walkthrough: Belgian points to French, one of Belgium's languages, so who becomes QUI.
annotation.definitionFit: Colloquial describes informal, conversational diction.

entries.clue: Poor old Scandinavian receiving pardon (3-5)

indicators.note: the Scandinavian word takes the pardon word inside

blocks.note: eh? = pardon?, asking someone to repeat

annotation.surface: An impoverished elderly Norseman is granted a pardon.
annotation.walkthrough: Pardon is the spoken request to repeat, not a legal release.
annotation.definitionFit: One-horse means small and poorly provided, as in a one-horse town.

entries.clue: Daughter’s wiped out by sedatives in possession (9)

indicators.note: D is removed from the sedatives word

blocks.note: downers are sedative drugs; lose the D
in and hip both mean fashionable

annotation.surface: A daughter has been knocked out by sedatives while in possession of them.
annotation.walkthrough: In possession reads as one phrase, but in is wordplay (HIP) and possession alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ownership and possession both mean having something as your own.

entries.clue: Appeal against book supporter censoring hard subject reference (6)

indicators.note: the H is cut out of the supporter word

annotation.surface: A publisher appeals against a bookseller who censored a difficult subject.
annotation.walkthrough: Subject reference sounds like a library term; it describes a reflexive pronoun, which points back to the subject of a sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: Itself is a reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject.

entries.clue: Wheeler-dealer disposing of small island with a show of emotion (8)

indicators.note: to dispose of something is to get rid of it, so the S is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a shyster is an unscrupulous operator

annotation.surface: A property speculator sells off a little island and makes a scene about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Small island looks like one thing to lose, but small (S) is dropped and island (I) is added.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hysteria names an outburst of uncontrolled feeling, whether panic, grief or laughter.

entries.clue: Key information guided claims (6)

indicators.note: the guided word takes the information word into it

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information

annotation.surface: Crucial intelligence steered someone's assertions.
annotation.walkthrough: Key is the explanatory table on a map, which is also called its legend.
annotation.definitionFit: A map's key, explaining its symbols, is called the legend.

entries.clue: Extremely slow golf amateur almost everyone stood up (7)

indicators.note: ALL loses its last letter
in a down entry, standing letters up turns them round

blocks.note: G = golf in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An amateur golfer plays so slowly that everyone is left standing.
annotation.walkthrough: Stood up looks like people waiting, but it turns LAIC-AL round.
annotation.definitionFit: Glacial means extremely slow, like a moving glacier.

entries.clue: Fabulous maiden having rejected frilly skirt this short (8)

indicators.note: the frilly word is turned back
the turned letters go round the next piece
THIS loses its last letter

blocks.note: M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

annotation.surface: A fairytale maiden turns down a skirt because it is too short and frilly.
annotation.walkthrough: Skirt is a verb, to go round the edge, not the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its old sense means belonging to fable: mythical.

entries.clue: Pizza toppings in Calabria acknowledge local region (7)

indicators.note: the tops, first letters, of the next three words

annotation.surface: Calabrians credit the pizza toppings to their own part of Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: Toppings sounds like cheese and ham, but in a down entry the tops of words are their first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the calzone is a kind of pizza folded over into a half-moon with the filling sealed inside.

entries.clue: Digitally extended audio recording of Debussy? (6)

indicators.note: we hear the name rather than read it

annotation.surface: A digitally remastered extended recording of Debussy's music is released.
annotation.walkthrough: Digitally looks like studio technology, but digits are fingers and toes: something clawed has claws on them. Debussy stands for his first name, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Clawed means having claws, extensions of the digits.

entries.clue: Doctor cutting tremor at emergency room with a large lozenge? (13)

indicators.note: the doctor cuts into the tremor word

blocks.note: to quail is to tremble with fear

annotation.surface: A doctor in A&E prescribes a big throat lozenge for a patient's shaking.
annotation.walkthrough: Lozenge looks like a throat sweet, but the question mark flags the geometric sense: a diamond shape, one kind of four-sided figure.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the diamond shape called a lozenge has four straight sides.

entries.clue: Bit of a ladder in stocking one could be regretting (5)

indicators.note: the ladder word stocks, holds, the one

blocks.note: a rung is one step of a ladder

annotation.surface: Someone who finds a ladder in their stocking might well be sorry.
annotation.walkthrough: The ladder in a stocking is a run in the hose, but here ladder means the kind with steps, and stocking is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rue is to feel sorrow over something done, so ruing is regretting.

entries.clue: Capture minds by succeeding (4)

indicators.note: the capture word looks after, holds, the by letter

annotation.surface: A persuasive speaker wins people over by being successful.
annotation.walkthrough: By becomes X from the multiplication sign, read as three by four.
annotation.definitionFit: Next means following, succeeding in order.

entries.clue: Retired gentleman greeting hosts from Dublin? (5)

indicators.note: the whole assembly goes back, reading right to left
the greeting word holds the gentleman word

annotation.surface: A retired gentleman welcomes visitors who have come over from Dublin.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags from Dublin as an example: a Dubliner is Irish, not every Irish person a Dubliner.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dublin is the capital of Ireland, so its people and things are one instance of the nationality.

entries.clue: Trying Morris dancing beset by calamity (9)

indicators.note: the letters of Morris move about
the calamity word surrounds the jumbled letters

annotation.surface: Attempting Morris dancing ends in disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is English folk dance with bells and sticks; here it only jumbles MORRIS.
annotation.definitionFit: Trying as an adjective means causing worry or annoyance: worrisome.

entries.clue: Probably missing middle notebook leaf (4,3)

indicators.note: the middle letters are taken out

annotation.surface: A notebook probably has a page missing from the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: Leaf looks like a page of the notebook, but it is a plant's leaf: the floating one of a water lily.
annotation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily.

entries.clue: Have workers for university succeeded in imposing raise? (7)

indicators.note: an instruction to make the change that follows
the workers stand in place of the university and succeeded letters
the swap happens inside the imposing word

annotation.surface: Do staff at a university get a pay rise when they take on more duties?
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pay-rise question; the definition is raise used as a verb, to increase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, verb for verb: to augment something is to make it greater, as a raise augments a salary.
